question: In March 2025, according to the Ministry of Earth Sciences, how many earthquakes were recorded in India during November 2024 to February 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**159**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, a total of **159 earthquakes** were recorded in India during the period from **November 2024 to February 2025**.
 
• This data highlights the seismic activity recorded over four months, reflecting the geological dynamism of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **Indian Plate** is tectonically active, interacting with the Eurasian Plate, which contributes to frequent seismic activities, especially in the Himalayan region and other fault lines across the country.
 
• The recorded number of earthquakes indicates the need for **preparedness and safety measures** in regions prone to high seismic activity.
 
• Other options provided in the question, such as **136, 197, and 213**, are incorrect as they do not match the official data released by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's Seismic Zones:**

 
 
• India is divided into **four seismic zones** based on the level of seismic risk: Zone II (low risk), Zone III (moderate risk), Zone IV (high risk), and Zone V (very high risk).
 
• Zone V includes regions like **Himalayas, northeastern states, Rann of Kutch, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**, which are highly prone to earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Earthquake Monitoring:**
 
 
• The **National Centre for Seismology (NCS)**, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is responsible for monitoring seismic activity in India.
 
• It operates a network of **seismological observatories** equipped with advanced instruments to record and analyze earthquakes in real time.
 
 
 
• **Preparedness and Safety Measures:**
 
 
• Regions prone to earthquakes require **strict enforcement of building codes** and the use of earthquake-resistant designs in infrastructure.
 
• Public awareness campaigns and **disaster response drills** are essential to minimize casualties during seismic events.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• India has experienced several major earthquakes in the past, such as the **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, **Kashmir earthquake (2005)**, and **Bihar-Nepal earthquake (2015)**.
 
• These events emphasize the importance of proactive measures to mitigate the impact of future earthquakes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Plate Tectonics:**

 
 
• India lies at the junction of the **Indian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate**, making it prone to frequent seismic activity.
 
• The **collision of these plates** is responsible for the upliftment of the Himalayas and the associated seismicity in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Magnitude and Intensity:**
 
 
• Earthquakes are measured in terms of **magnitude (Richter Scale)** and **intensity (Modified Mercalli Scale)**.
 
• While magnitude measures the energy released at the source, intensity measures the impact felt on the surface.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• India is part of the **Ring of Fire**, a seismically active region encircling the Pacific Ocean, though its primary seismic activity is due to the Himalayan collision zone.
 
• Countries like Japan and Indonesia also face frequent seismic events due to similar tectonic activities.
